combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: The single most common ingredient in GHB emergencies. Potentiation is steep and unpredictable — a dose that was fine sober can mean unrousable unconsciousness with a drink on board, and GHB's dose-response curve is already the steepest in common use. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Opioids
combinations.description: Two independent brakes on breathing, pressed at once. Respiratory depression stacks, and GHB's abrupt onset means the window between fine and unresponsive is minutes. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Benzodiazepines
combinations.description: Additive CNS depression on top of GHB's steep curve — profound sedation and respiratory depression with no reliable way to titrate. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Other depressants
combinations.description: Gabapentinoids, sedating antihistamines, sleep medications — anything sedating narrows GHB's already-narrow margin. If a combination is unavoidable, reduce the GHB dose substantially and never dose alone.
